title: The Tax Audit
sceneText: The inspector closes the ledger and begins putting his folder in order. It looks as though he is leaving.

choices.text: It is getting late — stay and have some lunch

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler to stay for lunch. He did not stay.

choices.resultText:
{@timothy}“No need,” he says. “I eat in town.”

He puts the folder under his arm. He has probably said that sentence dozens of times this year: every steward on every estate asks him to a meal, and every meal would make what he has to write afterwards harder to write.

{@timothy}“I shall be back next quarter.” He pushes the door open and goes.

choices.text: Do the other estates around here have this in their books too?

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler about the other estates’ books.

choices.resultText:
He stops and looks at you for two seconds.

{@timothy}“The other estates’ books are the other estates’ business.”

He does not say it heavily, but there is no room left behind it. He fastens the folder and goes to the door.

{@timothy}“Baron von Alder’s last family steward never asked me a question of that kind.”

The door closes.

effects.logEntry: You asked Kessler what that payment was, technically.

choices.resultText:
His hands stop.

{@timothy}“Technically it is nothing at all,” he says. “The sum is too small, the summary states a purpose, there is a record of who handled it. It does not constitute concealment. It does not constitute misappropriation. It does not even constitute negligence.”

{@timothy}“If you are asking me what it is” — he shuts the clasp on the folder — “it is give where there ought not to be any.”

He stands up.

{@timothy}“That is not illegal. I have seen worse. I have seen more elegant. This is in the middle.”

At the door he stops.

{@timothy}“Baron von Alder’s last family steward. I dealt with him three years,” he says. “His books were cleaner than yours.”

He closes the door and goes.
